text:
Situation: Enalapril maleate 10 mg tablets are not on FDA's drug shortage list as of 2026-10-21. Corvale East holds 507 tablets (44.4 days on hand at 11.4 tablets per day). Corvale General holds 262 tablets (18.8 days on hand at 14 tablets per day). The current labeler for NDC 71335960403 is Bryant Ranch Prepack (FEI 1000519407), a relabel/repack operation inspected 2026-07-16 and classified VAI. FDA records show an OAI classification for that plant in 2009 followed by multiple VAI inspections through 2026.

Why (FDA record): FDA's shortage list does not include enalapril maleate as of 2026-10-21. The Bryant Ranch Prepack facility received a VAI classification on 2026-07-16; its history includes an OAI in 2009 and subsequent VAI inspections.

Our position: Supply at Corvale General is below the 30-day target. Corvale East is above target but cannot cover both sites indefinitely. No FDA shortage declaration exists to trigger allocation programs. Alternate manufacturers are not on FDA's shortage list, but their labels do not identify a verifiable plant.

Recommended actions:
1. Buyer to request quotes and lead times from Amici Pharma, Inc. (ranked option 1); requires P&T approval before purchase.
2. Buyer to request quotes and lead times from Bausch Health US LLC (ranked option 2); requires P&T approval before purchase.
3. Buyer to request quotes and lead times from Bausch Health US, LLC (ranked option 3); requires P&T approval before purchase.
4. Buyer to request quotes and lead times from Chartwell RX, LLC (ranked option 4); requires P&T approval before purchase.
5. Buyer to request quotes and lead times from Coupler LLC (ranked option 5); requires P&T approval before purchase.
6. Buyer to monitor FDA shortage list weekly and report changes to P&T; no additional approval needed for monitoring.

Not recommended: Initiating therapeutic interchange or dose changes without P&T clinical review. Purchasing from alternate suppliers without confirmed plant identification and P&T approval.
